body.statement: For every \(0<\alpha\le1/4\), there exists an interval in \(\mathfrak C_\alpha\), measurable from \(D\), obtained by minimizing over \(J\), applying the observed-data block Horvitz--Thompson estimator on \(J\), and adding omitted contrast allowance \(\sum_{l\notin J}w_l\), whose length is at most \(2\min\{1,\rho_\alpha(w,q)\}\).
body.justification: Trimming prevents a low-weight, astronomically rare block from making the global interval inconsistent through inverse-probability amplification.
body.gap: KandirosHarshawSavje2026 removes difficult conflict-graph vertices for mean-squared error; this fixed-design procedure protects omitted causal contrast and retains finite-sample coverage.
body.consumer: The interval tells practitioners when to bias-protect a negligible rare block rather than report an explosive inverse-probability radius.
